message.content:
Explore /home/cis/windows/realstate — a Next.js 16 / React 19 real estate site. I need a thorough map of ALL existing 3D, WebGL, animation, and motion infrastructure, because we're about to massively expand the 3D/animation surface of this site.

Search breadth: very thorough.

Read and report in detail on:
1. `components/hero/hero-canvas.tsx`, `hero-scene.tsx`, `home-hero.tsx`, `scroll-frame-sequence.tsx` — what each does, what Three.js/R3F APIs they use, how they compose.
2. `components/webgl-boundary.tsx` and `components/lazy-mount.tsx` — the gating/suspense/error-boundary patterns.
3. `components/projects/master-plan-3d.tsx`, `master-plan.tsx`, `pannellum-tour.tsx` — the 3D massing and 360 panorama implementations.
4. `components/motion/*` — fade-in-view.tsx, motion-features.ts, motion-provider.tsx, scroll-reveal.tsx. Report exactly what animation approach is used (the README claims Framer Motion was removed in favor of IntersectionObserver+CSS, but framer-motion IS in package.json — verify which is actually true by reading the imports).
5. `components/providers/lenis-provider.tsx` and `reduced-motion-provider.tsx`.
6. Any GSAP usage — grep for `gsap` and `@gsap/react` imports across the repo.
7. `scripts/generate-frames.mjs` and `scripts/extract-frames.md` — what the scroll frame sequence pipeline is.
8. What's actually in `/public` — list the directory tree with file sizes, especially any images, models (.glb/.gltf), videos, or frame sequences.

For each file, report: exact import list, key exported components/functions, the props interface, and how it's mounted (client vs server component). Quote the important code sections verbatim. I need enough detail to plan a major 3D overhaul without re-reading these files.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

     2	
     3	A quiet-luxury marketing site for a mid-to-premium residential developer in
     4	Ahmedabad. Multi-project brand site, not a single-project microsite.
     5	
     6	The full brief — market research, design system, legal obligations, phased
     7	build order — lives in [`CLAUDE.md`](./CLAUDE.md). Read it before changing
     8	anything visual or legal.
     9	
    10	## Getting started
    11	
    12	```bash
    13	npm install
    14	npm run dev     # http://localhost:3000
    15	npm run build   # production build
    16	npm run lint
    17	```
    18	
    19	## The config file
    20	
    21	Everything client-specific lives in **`lib/site-config.ts`** — brand name,
    22	phone, WhatsApp number, email, office address, geo coordinates, socials, RERA
    23	identity and the festive-offer switch. Nothing else in the codebase hardcodes
    24	these. To rebrand the site, edit that one file.
    25	
    26	Two fields deserve care:
    27	
    28	- `whatsapp` must be **E.164 digits only** (`919999999999`, no `+` or spaces) —
    29	  that is what the `wa.me` deep-link format requires.
    30	- `rera.promoterNumber` ships as `DEMO-PENDING`. **Never replace it with an
    31	  invented number.** RERA Act §59 attaches penalties of up to 10% of estimated
    32	  project cost to the advertisement itself, and a website is an advertisement.
    33	
    34	Set `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` in the environment to control canonical URLs,
    35	`metadataBase` and Open Graph URLs. It falls back to `https://example.com`.
    36

    38	
    39	All five build phases from `CLAUDE.md` §16 are implemented.
    40	
    41	**Content & data**
    42	- `lib/data.ts` is the CMS seam. It reads from `lib/placeholders/` today and every
    43	  function is async, returning the shapes a Sanity query would. Wiring the CMS
    44	  means rewriting that one file — no component changes.
    45	- Six demo projects, six micro-markets, twelve amenities, three testimonials,
    46	  three long-form insight posts.
    47	
    48	**Pages** — home, projects listing (URL-synced filters), project detail,
    49	locations index + six corridor guides, amenities, gallery, about/legacy,
    50	NRI corner, insights + three articles, contact, channel partners, careers,
    51	RERA disclosure, privacy, terms, 404.
    52	
    53	**Tools**
    54	- Floor-plan viewer: schematic SVG per configuration, wheel/drag zoom and pan,
    55	  keyboard controls (`+`, `-`, `0`, arrows), north compass rotated to the unit's
    56	  facing, room dimensions derived from real carpet area.
    57	- EMI calculator: reducing-balance amortisation, four live inputs.
    58	- Cost sheet: agreement value, GST, Gujarat stamp duty, registration,
    59	  maintenance advance — server-rendered so it stays crawlable.
    60	- Brochure: ungated download plus an optional name-and-phone gate.
    61	- Gallery lightbox: Embla, keyboard-navigable, Escape to close.
    62	
    63	**3D** — WebGL hero, clickable master-plan massing, and a 360° panorama, all
    64	gated behind `lib/webgl.ts` (real context probe, pointer type, viewport,
    65	cores/memory, reduced-motion) and wrapped in `components/webgl-boundary.tsx`.
    66	Every one sits over content that already works without it.

    69	per-project OG images via `next/og`, and JSON-LD throughout:
    70	`RealEstateAgent` site-wide, `Apartment`/`SingleFamilyResidence` + `Offer`,
    71	`Place`, `Article`, `BreadcrumbList` and `FAQPage`.
    72	
    73	## Measured performance
    74	
    75	Production build, Lighthouse mobile, on a developer laptop — **not CI**. Expect
    76	±5 points of run-to-run variance; stop every dev server first, or scores drop
    77	by 15.

    82	| `/projects` | 98 | 100 | 100 | 2.1s | 0 |
    83	| `/projects/[slug]` | 86–90 | 100 | 100 | 3.0s | 0 |
    84	| `/locations/[slug]` | 95 | 100 | 100 | 2.9s | 0 |
    85	| `/amenities` | 97 | 100 | 100 | 2.6s | 0 |
    86	| `/gallery` | 90 | 100 | 100 | 2.8s | 0 |
    87	| `/about` | 90 | 100 | 100 | 2.9s | 0 |

    89	Desktop is 100 across performance, accessibility and best practices.
    90	Accessibility is 100 on every page measured.

    94	  far the heaviest page — ~142KB of HTML and eight interactive blocks. Every one
    95	  of those blocks is already dynamically imported.

    97	  is hero body text and the delay is the webfont swap; `size-adjust` fallback
    98	  tuning is the next lever.

   102	real score.

   105

   107	and §4 records why:

   109	- **MapLibre → hand-drawn SVG.** ~200KB gzip and a keyed tile provider, versus

   112	  renderer bought nothing.

   115	  time. Removing it moved amenities from 74 to 97 and the project page from 65
   116	  to 88.

   119	
   120	- Server Components by default. `"use client"` only where a hook or listener

   125	  the result: tailwind-merge treats same-prefix classes as conflicting. That
   126	  collision is why the class is not called `.text-luxury`.

---

## 3. Competitive Teardown

**Global luxury sites (what feels expensive):** scroll-as-storytelling; one hard idea executed
cleanly instead of stacked effects; WebGL for *atmosphere, not spectacle*; confident editorial
typography; weighted smooth scroll; invisible transitions. 2026 award winners have largely abandoned
heavy video backgrounds (<8%) and full-page hero-image-with-overlay (<12%).
Refs: Awwwards, FWA, CSS Design Awards, Godly, Lapa Ninja; Iventions, ERA/Silver Pinewood (Vide Infra).

**Indian developer sites (Lodha, Godrej, Sobha, DLF, Prestige, Oberoi, Hiranandani, Mahindra
Lifespaces, Rustomjee, Piramal, Total Environment, Embassy)**
- *Good:* strong brand hero, project filters, floor plans + virtual tours, sustainability messaging,
  testimonials, awards, legacy narrative.
- *Bad:* aggressive pop-up lead gates, forms demanding phone before showing anything, slow hero video,
  generic stock photography, no floor-plan zoom, no dated construction updates, no pricing
  transparency, broken mobile, template-y WordPress builds, weak local SEO.

**Portals (99acres, MagicBricks, Housing.com, NoBroker, Square Yards):** buyers expect map search,
filters (BHK/budget/possession/RERA), EMI calculators, locality guides + price trends, verified
photos, instant contact. **Match or beat portals** on filtering, location intelligence, transparency
and speed — while delivering a brand experience portals cannot.

---

## 4. Tech Stack (all free / open-source)

- **Next.js 16** (App Router, TypeScript, React 19, Server Components by default, Turbopack).
  Typed routes are on by default — a `<Link>` to a route that does not exist fails the build,
  so stub pages must land before the links that point at them.
- **Tailwind CSS v4** + **shadcn/ui** (Radix primitives)
- **Framer Motion** (component reveals and micro-interactions) + **GSAP 3.13+** with ScrollTrigger
  (scroll-linked headline reveals) + **Lenis** (smooth scroll).
  Framer must be used through `LazyMotion` with the `domAnimation` feature set and the `m`
  primitive, never the full `motion` component — the difference is roughly 150–300ms of blocking
  time on pages carrying a dozen reveals. `components/motion/motion-provider.tsx` sets `strict`
  so a stray `motion` import fails loudly.
  - GSAP is **100% free since 30 Apr 2025** (Webflow announcement), including all former Club plugins,
    commercial use covered. No paid dependency remains in the motion stack.
- **React Three Fiber** + `@react-three/drei` + `@react-three/postprocessing` (tasteful WebGL only)
- **Embla Carousel** (galleries), **react-hook-form + Zod** (forms), **schema-dts** (typed JSON-LD)
- **Sanity CMS** (projects/units/amenities/locations/testimonials/blog), Studio embedded at `/studio`.
  Alternative: Payload v3 (self-host). Sanity recommended for a non-technical builder team.
- Email: **Resend** (fallback Nodemailer). Spam: **Cloudflare Turnstile** + honeypot
- Images/video: `next/image` + **ImageKit** (or Cloudinary) free tier
- Maps: **MapLibre GL** + OpenStreetMap (Google Maps only if reviews/embeds needed).
  Mounted on intersection behind a server-rendered SVG corridor map, so the ~200KB library never
  sits on the critical path and a blocked tile host still leaves a usable map.
  **Before launch:** set `NEXT_PUBLIC_MAP_TILE_URL` to a provider you hold an account with —
  OSM's public tiles are not licensed for production traffic.
- 360 tours: **Pannellum** (~21KB, MIT) — UMD, so imported inside an effect on intersection rather
  than at module scope. Alt: Marzipano, Photo Sphere Viewer
- Analytics: Vercel Analytics + GA4 via GTM; Meta Pixel for retargeting
- Hosting: **Vercel**. Bundle watch: `@next/bundle-analyzer`

```bash
cd builder-site
npm i gsap @gsap/react framer-motion lenis three @react-three/fiber @react-three/drei \

# Sanity: npm create sanity@latest -- --template clean --create-project "Builder Site" --dataset production
```
=========== §7 ===========

---

## 7. WebGL / Three.js Guardrails

Treat the viewport as a cinematic film set, not a toy.

- **Materials:** PBR `MeshStandardMaterial` with real roughness/metalness/normal maps (e.g.
  metalness 0.8 / roughness 0.2). Never flat unlit meshes.
- **Lighting:** architectural-studio setup — soft ambient occlusion, subtle directional light with
  shadow mapping (`<ambientLight intensity={0.5} />` + `<directionalLight castShadow />`).
- **Post-processing:** subtle SSR, controlled bloom, chromatic aberration, film grain, vignette.
- **Camera:** no jarring cuts or free-roam (motion sickness). Dampened lerp / GSAP drone-like reveals.
- **Budgets:** hero scene <100k triangles, <30 draw calls; DPR capped at 1.5.
- **Assets:** Draco/meshopt-compressed GLTF; KTX2 or WebP textures (GPU-direct, no CPU decode).
- **Memory:** never allocate inside `useFrame`/rAF (`new THREE.Vector3()` → GC stutter). Instantiate
  vectors/matrices once and recycle. Pause rAF when offscreen (IntersectionObserver) and on tab blur.
- **Threading:** offload the Three.js pipeline to a Web Worker via **OffscreenCanvas** so shader
  compilation/geometry parsing never blocks the main thread (keeps INP <200ms).
- **Loading:** wrap `<Canvas>` in `dynamic(() => import(...), { ssr:false })` — never block LCP.
  Reserve container dimensions with CSS `aspect-ratio` to prevent CLS.
- **Fallbacks:** mobile / low-power / reduced-motion get a high-res static WebP or `<video poster>`
  instead of the 3D scene.
- **Progressive enhancement is mandatory:** real H1, body copy and links live in server-rendered HTML
  behind/around the canvas. Bots read HTML, not WebGL pixels.

---

## 8. Page-by-Page Spec

**HOME** — (1) cinematic hero: subtle R3F scene or poster + muted-autoplay video, editorial headline
with SplitText reveal, real H1 in server HTML, static fallback on mobile. (2) Trust bar: years/legacy,
projects delivered, sq ft delivered, on-time possession, RERA badge. (3) Featured projects
(Ongoing/Completed/Upcoming tabs). (4) Why us. (5) Micro-market map teaser. (6) NRI strip.
(7) Testimonials/video. (8) Insights teaser. (9) Conditional festive-offer banner. (10) Contact/WhatsApp CTA.
Sticky mobile bar: Call | WhatsApp | Enquire.

**PROJECTS LISTING** — filters (status, micro-market, BHK, budget, possession, RERA-registered, Vastu
facing); card grid (image, name, location, BHK, starting price or "Price on request", RERA badge,
status chip); URL-synced filter state, async filtering with no reload; ISR. Map-based browse.

=========== §6 motion tokens ===========
- If an image adds no emotional or informational value, delete it and leave negative space. Let images
  breathe; never edge-to-edge collages.
- Copy sells lifestyle, status and neighbourhood culture — minimal, sophisticated, zero hype. Lead
  with brand philosophy before dumping listings.

### Motion tokens
- Micro 150–200ms · UI 250–350ms · section reveals 400–600ms. **Never exceed 500ms** for interface
  animation; snappy beats slow.
- Easings: entrance `cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1)`; transition `cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1)`;
  Framer default `[0.25,0.1,0.25,1]`.
- Animate composite properties only (opacity, transform) → 60fps.
- GSAP ScrollTrigger for pinned/scroll-linked sequences + SplitText headline reveals; Framer Motion
  for component/page micro-interactions; Lenis (lerp ~0.1); View Transitions API for routes where
  supported.
- **Always honor `prefers-reduced-motion`** — disable Lenis, reduce GSAP to ≤300ms fades. Disable
  smooth scroll on touch if INP suffers.
- Converts: scroll-linked reveals, parallax within masks, horizontal galleries, sticky section
  transitions, tasteful text-mask reveals. Avoid: gimmicky cursors, motion that delays content,
  autoplay audio, chaotically spinning 3D models.

### Accessibility
WCAG 2.1 AA contrast, keyboard nav, visible focus, form labels, alt text, reduced-motion respected.

- **Memory:** never allocate inside `useFrame`/rAF (`new THREE.Vector3()` → GC stutter). Instantiate
  vectors/matrices once and recycle. Pause rAF when offscreen (IntersectionObserver) and on tab blur.
- **Threading:** offload the Three.js pipeline to a Web Worker via **OffscreenCanvas** so shader
  compilation/geometry parsing never blocks the main thread (keeps INP <200ms).
- **Loading:** wrap `<Canvas>` in `dynamic(() => import(...), { ssr:false })` — never block LCP.
  Reserve container dimensions with CSS `aspect-ratio` to prevent CLS.
- **Fallbacks:** mobile / low-power / reduced-motion get a high-res static WebP or `<video poster>`
  instead of the 3D scene.
- **Progressive enhancement is mandatory:** real H1, body copy and links live in server-rendered HTML
  behind/around the canvas. Bots read HTML, not WebGL pixels.

---

## 8. Page-by-Page Spec

**HOME** — (1) cinematic hero: subtle R3F scene or poster + muted-autoplay video, editorial headline
with SplitText reveal, real H1 in server HTML, static fallback on mobile. (2) Trust bar: years/legacy,
projects delivered, sq ft delivered, on-time possession, RERA badge. (3) Featured projects
(Ongoing/Completed/Upcoming tabs). (4) Why us. (5) Micro-market map teaser. (6) NRI strip.
(7) Testimonials/video. (8) Insights teaser. (9) Conditional festive-offer banner. (10) Contact/WhatsApp CTA.
Sticky mobile bar: Call | WhatsApp | Enquire.

**PROJECTS LISTING** — filters (status, micro-market, BHK, budget, possession, RERA-registered, Vastu
facing); card grid (image, name, location, BHK, starting price or "Price on request", RERA badge,
status chip); URL-synced filter state, async filtering with no reload; ISR. Map-based browse.

=========== §6 motion tokens ===========
- If an image adds no emotional or informational value, delete it and leave negative space. Let images
  breathe; never edge-to-edge collages.
- Copy sells lifestyle, status and neighbourhood culture — minimal, sophisticated, zero hype. Lead
  with brand philosophy before dumping listings.

### Motion tokens
- Micro 150–200ms · UI 250–350ms · section reveals 400–600ms. **Never exceed 500ms** for interface
  animation; snappy beats slow.
- Easings: entrance `cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1)`; transition `cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1)`;
  Framer default `[0.25,0.1,0.25,1]`.
- Animate composite properties only (opacity, transform) → 60fps.
- GSAP ScrollTrigger for pinned/scroll-linked sequences + SplitText headline reveals; Framer Motion
  for component/page micro-interactions; Lenis (lerp ~0.1); View Transitions API for routes where
  supported.
- **Always honor `prefers-reduced-motion`** — disable Lenis, reduce GSAP to ≤300ms fades. Disable
  smooth scroll on touch if INP suffers.
- Converts: scroll-linked reveals, parallax within masks, horizontal galleries, sticky section
  transitions, tasteful text-mask reveals. Avoid: gimmicky cursors, motion that delays content,
  autoplay audio, chaotically spinning 3D models.

### Accessibility
WCAG 2.1 AA contrast, keyboard nav, visible focus, form labels, alt text, reduced-motion respected.
